what_this_file_is: Every piece of third-party code that ends up INSIDE one of the binaries the Windows
installer ships, with the licence it is under and the exact file the licence was read
copies every licence text named here into the payload, and writes openDAQ-NOTICE.txt
from it. Nothing here is guessed: every entry names the file whose SPDX identifier or
licence text was read, and the linker input or #include that puts the code in the box.
why_it_exists: openDAQ-NOTICE.txt used to name openDAQ under Apache-2.0 and nothing else, while
modules/ref_fb_module-64-3.module.dll statically links kissfft under BSD-3-Clause and
SFML 3.0.2 with FreeType. BSD-3-Clause clause 2 and the FreeType Licence both require a
credit line in the documentation of a binary redistribution, so the shipped installer
was redistributing code it did not credit.
how_the_linkage_was_established: For every archive linked into a bundled binary: the MSBuild link.read.1.tlog under the
openDAQ build tree, which records the exact set of .lib files the linker consumed. The
staging script re-reads those tlogs and fails if a bundled binary consumed a library no
entry below claims. For header-only libraries, which leave no linker input: the #include
in the openDAQ (or quackoscope host) source that compiles them into the binary.

roots.opendaq_source: the openDAQ source checkout, six directories above manifest.module_path
roots.opendaq_build: the openDAQ build tree, two directories above manifest.module_path; holds __external/src and _deps
